entities.name: Federal Air Transport Agency
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Federal Air Transport Agency, established in 2004, serves as the regulatory body overseeing civil aviation in Russia, with its headquarters located on Leningradsky Avenue in Moscow. This institution emerged during a pivotal period of post-Soviet transformation in aviation, directly influencing the modernization and safety standards of the Russian aviation sector. Under the leadership of Director Alexander Neradko, the agency has been crucial in navigating the complexities of both domestic and international air transport, ensuring compliance with international aviation regulations and enhancing the safety of air travel across the vast expanse of Russia.

The establishment of the Federal Air Transport Agency can be traced back to the increasing need for a cohesive regulatory framework following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. With a significant rise in air traffic and a need for modernization, the agency was tasked with implementing reforms to improve air safety and efficiency. Key achievements include the introduction of stricter safety regulations and the promotion of state-of-the-art technology in Russian aircraft. In its early years, the agency focused on re-establishing international partnerships and fostering collaboration with global aviation bodies, which was essential for the reintegration of Russian airlines into the global market.

The legacy of the Federal Air Transport Agency is visible in the evolution of Russian civil aviation, which has seen substantial increases in passenger numbers and improvements in service quality. The agency’s regulatory framework laid the groundwork for the expansion of airlines such as Aeroflot and helped facilitate Russia's participation in international aviation agreements. Furthermore, the agency has influenced the broader economic landscape by supporting the aviation industry, which plays a critical role in connecting various regions of Russia, thus promoting economic development and tourism.
